newsitem.title: USA: Micron sees Q1 revs flat to above Q4 revs.
newsitem.headline: Micron sees Q1 revs flat to above Q4 revs.

text.p: Micron Technology Inc said Wednesday that Wall Street estimates of flat to slightly higher revenues for the company's fiscal first quarter, ended November, compared to the fourth quarter were reasonable.

Speaking to investors at the Montgomery Securities Conference here, Vice President of Corporate Affairs Kipp Bedard said the sequential growth in memory bits shipped, a key measure of volume for the chip maker, was in the 20-25 percent range for the first quarter, above the company's initial projection of bit growth in the low teens.
Micron reported revenues of $700.5 million in the fourth quarter, ended August 31. It expects to report first quarter results next Monday.
The Boise, Idaho-based chip maker declined to project financial results for the first quarter, but Bedard said the company's balance sheet is strong.
"I think people will be surprised by how good our balance sheet looks," he said.
He said it's not unusual to see pricing pressure for Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) chips following the Christmas period.
"We're at the bottom," he said, adding that the low point in DRAM pricing began last summer and it normally takes six months to a year for prices to rebound.
"I don't know if we're headed into another period of DRAM pricing (pressure) or not," he said.
He also said the company expects prices for 16-meg chips to decline to $5-$6 by summer, 1997.

Bedard said there has been "very good demand" for memory chips even in the last week, but he cautioned that demand can drop by about 40 percent after the Christmas season, even though corporate buying of computers looks like it will continue into the new year.
He said bit growth, the amount of total memory capacity shipped by the industry, rose nearly 80 percent in 1996, and he expects growth to be higher than that in 1997.
